NEW YORK, Oct. 08, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- The Board of Trustees (the "Board") of Simplify Exchange Traded Funds (the "Trust") has determined that it is in the best interests of shareholders to liquidate the Simplify Tax Aware Diversified Income Strategy ETF (DINE), the Simplify Tax Aware Alternatives ETF (LQ), the Simplify NEXT Intangible Core Index ETF (NXTI), the Simplify VettaFi Private Credit Strategy ETF (PCR), and the Simplify Volt TSLA Revolution ETF (TESL) — each, a "Fund" and together the "Funds" — each a series of the Trust, following a recommendation by each Fund's investment adviser, Simplify Asset Management Inc.

The Board has determined to liquidate the Funds with the liquidation payment to their respective shareholders expected to take place on or about November 6, 2026 ("Liquidation Date"). After the close of business on October 30, 2026, the Funds will no longer accept creation orders. The last day of trading of the Funds will be October 30, 2026. Shareholders who do not sell their shares of a Fund before market close on October 30, 2026 will receive cash equal to the amount of the net asset value of their shares in their brokerage accounts, on or about the Liquidation Date. As calculated on the Liquidation Date, each Fund's net asset value will reflect certain closing costs not borne by the adviser, such as brokerage commissions. The costs borne by a Fund are not expected to be material. Once the distributions are complete, the Funds will terminate.

title: Cathie Wood’s ARK Sells $23.7M of Robinhood, Buys $27.8M of CoreWeave
detail:
Cathie Wood’s ARK Sells $23.7M of Robinhood, Buys $27.8M of CoreWeave
Editorial Staff
Thu, October 8, 2026 at 2:26 PM MDT 2 min read
HOOD
BTC
CRWV
MSFT
SPCX
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

ARK Invest, the firm led by Cathie Wood, sold shares of Robinhood Markets (NASDAQ: $HOOD) for a second straight day while adding to its stake in AI cloud provider CoreWeave (NASDAQ: $CRWV).

According to trade data posted by the ArkkDaily account on X, ARK sold 63,446 HOOD shares worth $7.1 million on Oct. 6, followed by 151,903 shares worth $16.6 million on Oct. 7. That totals 215,349 shares valued at about $23.7 million. Over the same two sessions, the firm bought 97,639 CRWV shares worth $8.9 million and 214,589 shares worth $18.9 million, a combined 312,228 shares and roughly $27.8 million.

Robinhood remains among ARK's largest holdings, according to StockCircle data. Its shares are down 28% over the past year and 7% over the past month. Johann Kerbrat, the company's senior vice president and general manager of crypto and international, disclosed that Robinhood recently added about $25 million of Bitcoin (CRYPTO: $BTC) to its corporate balance sheet.

CoreWeave began as a crypto miner before pivoting to AI infrastructure, after lower prices, higher power costs and reduced rewards cut into mining profits. The company buys or leases AI chips from Nvidia (NASDAQ: $NVDA), builds data centers around them and rents the computing capacity to clients including Microsoft (NASDAQ: $MSFT), Alphabet's (NASDAQ: $GOOGL) Google, Anthropic and OpenAI.

CoreWeave announced Wednesday that it is entering the Indian market through a collaboration with AdaniConneX. Its stock is down 40% over the past 12 months and 15% this month.

Wood has built her reputation on bets in both crypto and AI. She has said ARK was the first public asset manager to gain bitcoin exposure, in 2015, when the token traded below $500. Bitcoin now trades near $82,000, well under the peak above $126,000 it reached a year ago.

ARK's largest holdings also include Tesla (NASDAQ: $TSLA) and SpaceX (NASDAQ: $SPCX), per StockCircle. The two companies hold 11,509 and 18,712 BTC, respectively.

Shares of Robinhood (NASDAQ: HOOD) are trading at $107.01 while CoreWeave (NASDAQ: CRWV) is currently sitting at $81.58.

title: BYD Trades at 20 Times Earnings. Tesla Trades at 344. Here's Which One I'd Buy Today.
detail:
BYD Trades at 20 Times Earnings. Tesla Trades at 344. Here's Which One I'd Buy Today.
Jeff Siegel, The Motley Fool
Thu, October 8, 2026 at 11:50 AM MDT 5 min read
TSLA
002594.SZ
Trade Tesla on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Tesla (NASDAQ: TSLA) and BYD (OTC: BYDDY) are two of the largest electric vehicle manufacturers in the world. But if you own them, you're paying dramatically different prices for each dollar of profit these companies generate. BYD currently trades at roughly 20 times trailing earnings. Tesla trades at around 344 times earnings. That's a massive difference, particularly when you look at what the two companies are actually selling.

In September, BYD sold 463,561 new-energy vehicles (vehicles powered by an alternative to fossil fuels), up about 17% from a year earlier. Overseas passenger vehicle and pickup sales reached nearly 180,000, representing an increase of more than 150%. Tesla, meanwhile, delivered 486,532 vehicles during the entire third quarter. That was better than Wall Street expected and was certainly a modest improvement from Q2. But deliveries were still down roughly 2% from a year earlier.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

So why does Tesla command such a higher valuation on an earnings basis? Because the market isn't really valuing Tesla as a car company anymore. Let's see which stock is the better deal right now.

Image source: Getty Images.
Tesla is a bet on what comes next

At 344 times earnings, Tesla's existing automotive business can't justify the valuation on its own. The bull case increasingly rests on autonomous driving, robotaxis, artificial intelligence, energy storage, and Optimus humanoid robots. And there's huge potential here.

Tesla deployed 13.7 gigawatt-hours of energy storage products during the third quarter, up from 13.5 gigawatt-hours in Q2. And its robotaxi ambitions could eventually create an entirely new business model. If Tesla develops a large autonomous ride-hailing network and successfully commercializes Optimus, today's earnings could look almost irrelevant five or 10 years from now. But if you're buying Tesla today, you're already paying for a lot of that success.

A 344 price-to-earnings ratio means Tesla can't simply become a somewhat larger automaker. It needs businesses like autonomy and robotics to become enormous profit generators. That's possible. And in my opinion, probable. But it's still not 100% guaranteed.

BYD doesn't need nearly as much to go right

BYD offers a very different proposition. The company makes battery-electric vehicles and plug-in hybrids, manufactures its own batteries, and has built one of the most vertically integrated automotive businesses in the world. It's also rapidly expanding outside of China.

title: General Motors vs. Tesla: What Revenue Growth Trends Tell Investors About These Automotive Giants
detail:
General Motors vs. Tesla: What Revenue Growth Trends Tell Investors About These Automotive Giants
Robert Izquierdo, The Motley Fool
Thu, October 8, 2026 at 11:25 AM MDT 4 min read
GM
TSLA
PCG
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
General Motors: Maintaining Steady Revenue Scale

General Motors (NYSE:GM) primarily generates revenue by designing, manufacturing, and distributing trucks, sport utility vehicles, passenger cars, and automotive parts for retail consumers and commercial fleet operations, while also offering automotive financing, insurance solutions, and subscription-based connected services to customers worldwide.

It recently entered a multi-year global partnership with 3M to provide advanced materials for its racing team, while it also partnered with PG&E to launch a new residential charging bundle that provides California customers with home charging hardware and monthly bill credits.

Tesla: Experiencing Higher Revenue Growth and Volatility

Tesla (NASDAQ:TSLA) primarily earns revenue by developing, manufacturing, and directly selling electric passenger cars, commercial transport vehicles, and large-scale energy generation and storage systems, alongside offering post-sale vehicle maintenance services, retail merchandise, and automotive regulatory credits to global buyers.

It recently held a public launch event in Texas for its purpose-built Cybercab autonomous vehicle, and it secured a contract to supply 2,500 electric commercial tractors to a transportation coalition with initial deliveries expected to begin in the fourth quarter of 2026.

Why Revenue Matters for Investors

Revenue serves as a starting point to help investors understand the total amount of money a business brings in before deducting any operational expenses. This metric helps investors measure a company's overall size, market footprint, and long-term trajectory.
